newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar firms on rosier March trade data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar firms on rosier March trade data.

text.p: The Singapore dollar firmed against the dollar on Monday after Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) released better-than-expected March non-oil domestic exports figures.
According to the TDB, Singapore's non-oil domestic exports fell a nominal 2.1 percent year-on-year in March to Singapore $7.67 billion against a 7.9 percent drop in February.
The figures were better than a Reuter's forecast of an average drop of 4.5 percent in nominal terms, fuelling dealers hope for an economic recovery in the second-half of 1997.
After trading to a low of 1.4415 to the dollar, the Singapore dollar firmed to 1.4385 against the greenback at 0500 GMT after the release of the non-oil exports data.
The Singapore dollar was expected to hover around 1.4370/80 to the dollar in the afternoon, according to Andy Tan, general manager and economist at MMS International Ltd.
"We see scope for the dollar/Sing to test 1.4370/80 level," Tan told Reuters.
"If broken, the next support for the Singapore dollar will be at 1.4320 to the dollar," he said.
Tan felt it unlikely the Singapore dollar would firm beyond 1.4320 against the greenback.
"The trade figures were better than expected but not to the extent that would justify that kind of firmness," he said, adding that 1.4320 had been tested and sustained on numerous occasions.

TDB said in a statement the decline in exports was largely due to continuing problems in the electronics industry, which accounts for half of Singapore's manufacturing output and close to 60 percent of its non-oil exports.

TDB also said non-oil sales to the United States fell 10.6 percent to S$2.1 billion in March. The decrease was reflected in domestic exports of disk drives, computer parts and other electronics peripherals.
